references.text: Solomon's proverbs give the same wisdom: "Do not boast in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men. For it is better to be told, 'Come up here,' than to be put lower." Jesus' parable is a direct elaboration of this proverb. [ref:Prov 25:6-7|Proverbs 25:6-7]
Humility as a fundamental principle: "When pride comes, then comes shame, but wisdom is with the humble." [ref:Prov 11:2|Proverbs 11:2]

Warning against arrogance: "Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall. It is better to be lowly among the meek than to share plunder with the proud." [ref:Prov 16:18-19|Proverbs 16:18-19]

The immediate continuation of the parable, where Jesus advises taking the lowest seat so as to be invited higher, and summarizes the principle: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted." [ref:Lk 14:10-11|Luke 14:10-11]
Jesus warns against the scribes who seek the places of honor at banquets – an example of the behavior Jesus warns against here. [ref:Lk 20:46|Luke 20:46]
Jesus criticizes the Pharisees and the scribes because they love the places of honor at banquets and the best seats in the synagogues. [ref:Mt 23:6|Matthew 23:6]
Mark's parallel where Jesus warns against the scribes who seek the best places at banquets and the foremost seats in the synagogues. [ref:Mk 12:38-39|Mark 12:38-39]

Jesus pronounces a "woe" upon the Pharisees who love the chief seats in the synagogues and to be greeted respectfully in the marketplaces – the same theme of seeking honor and prominent positions. [ref:Lk 11:43|Luke 11:43]
James warns against showing partiality to the rich by giving them the best places, which reflects the theme of ranking and humility in social settings. [ref:Jas 2:1-4|James 2:1-4]
